Marginalization

/mar-jih-nul-ih-ZAY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Marginalization means the process of pushing a person or group to the edges of society, where they are treated as unimportant and denied real influence

Marginalization means the process of pushing a person or group to the edges of society, where they are treated as unimportant and denied real influence. Historians traced the marginalization of the immigrant dockworkers, who were barred from union meetings and passed over for every promotion.

Worked Example

The report found that the marginalization of rural towns in broadband planning left entire counties without a voice in decisions that shaped their own economies.

Marginalization fits because the rural towns are being pushed to the edge of the decision-making process — they are treated as unimportant and denied influence over broadband policy, even though the outcomes directly affect them.

How Marginalization Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

exclusion

exclusion: the act of shutting someone out of a group or activity

sidelining

sidelining: pushing someone out of the action or out of decisions

disempowerment

disempowerment: stripping a person or group of power or influence

Antonyms

inclusion

inclusion: deliberately bringing everyone into a group or process

empowerment

empowerment: giving a person or group power and confidence

How Strong Is It? — oversight → ostracism → marginalization

oversight vs. marginalization

oversight vs. marginalization: An oversight is weaker — it is a one-time accidental overlooking of someone, without marginalization's sense of an ongoing pattern that pushes people to the edge.

ostracism vs. marginalization

ostracism vs. marginalization: Ostracism is stronger — it is total, deliberate banishment from the group, going beyond marginalization's edge-of-the-room treatment to complete exclusion.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — margin

Root — margin: edge, border, brink (Latin margo, marginis)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to (adjective-forming)

Suffix — -iz(e)

Suffix — -iz(e): to make, to cause to become (verb-forming)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the act or process of (noun-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: The pieces stack up to 'the process of making someone edge-positioned': margin (edge) becomes marginal (at the edge), then marginalize (to push to the edge), then marginalization — the whole process of forcing people to the border of society where they can be ignored.

Use the root in a new word: marginal

Use the root in a new word: marginal: The family scraped by on marginal farmland at the edge of the valley, where the rocky soil barely produced a harvest.

Root Check

Word Choice

Academic / sociological

Marginalization belongs to formal writing about society, history, and policy — it names an ongoing process done to groups of people, not a single snub. In everyday conversation, people say a person was 'shut out' or 'sidelined' instead; save marginalization for essays, reports, and analysis.
